summary: If it were possible for a person in the world to be completely good, then that person would probably look a lot like Lan Sizhui. Jin Ling hadn’t thought it possible to be so polite or kind or beautiful. That sounded like something out of a myth, a children’s tale parents told their kids and or a fantasy teachers told their students. Something too good to be real.But Sizhui? Sizhui is good and real and Jin Ling loves him. Sizhui is serenity, is blue on white, clean sleeves and kind smiles. Sizhui holds a fist over his mouth when he laughs (really laughs, not just the nervous sound he makes when he stops Jingyi from punching him—and Sizhui always stops him) and sometimes his eyes will sparkle when he looks at Jin Ling. Mostly in apology, because of something someone’s done again, but also with kindness. Sizhui has kind eyes, warm eyes, eyes that sing to you and tell you you are loved. Jin Ling wants him to smile so badly it hurts.

summary: This was written as a gift for azure7539arts on Tumblr as part of the MDZS Network Gift Exchange. azure7539arts  :) I hope you enjoy this as much as I did writing it. ___Since MDZS is essentially set in the loose time frame of ancient China, and Christmas wasn't really a thing, I went with the New Year celebration for the holiday event. I thought it also fit their story since I set this as being the first New Year celebration that Lan WangJi and Wei WuXian celebrate together as an official, married couple. The New Year celebration is a time to look forward to the future and to be thankful for the blessings one has received through the previous year. It is a time to celebrate new beginnings, and considering what these two have gone through to get to a point of being happy together I found that concept truly fitting and appealing.

His husband sits motionless in the gliding chair, eyes vacantly staring out the lone window, the sheen of tear tracks lit up on his pale cheeks, illuminated by the soft glow of the bunny nightlight. title: Kiss Me Here, Again, Again
author: pastelaliens

relationships: Lan Zhan | Lan Wangji/Wei Ying | Wei Wuxian
summary:
Back then, when he’d been shaken from sleep during his reflective punishment and told, ‘The Yiling Patriarch is dead!’ To be suddenly awake and alive in a world that no longer held Wei Wuxian— no pain had ever come close or ever will. Even screaming his throat raw, even plucking the strings of his guqin down to the bone, even holding a brand too close to the fire before burning its design into his own skin— nothing, nothing, nothing to the fracturing of his heart.
And more than just loss, it had been regret.
“Back then, back then,” Wei Wuxian echoes in a sigh, the sound of it cutting through the memory. “Be here with me instead, Lan Zhan.” It isn’t dismissive but instead kindly coaxing, a guiding path to the present they now share. Here is Wei Wuxian, bright eyes and curling corners of a smile and heart open wide. Here is Lan Wangji, gathering it all to him, holding it as close as he always wished he could with a selfishness learned in loneliness. Here are the both of them, falling to the bed in a knot of limbs that only gets more tangled when someone tries to pull them apart. Here are the both of them, laid bare both in body and in love. summary: 铺垫结束，正式展开哨兵向导世界观。（lofter脑抽屏蔽存稿处）世界观介绍：1.扶桑树是力量源泉，其花粉飘散千里，能觉醒部分修真人士体内魁元（哨兵）或参宿（向导）能力。参宿更为稀少，数量为魁元的十分之一。魁元与参宿互相吸引并且能够通过气韵（向导素）辨别身份，每一个魁元参宿都有不同的气韵。2.魁元五感六觉强悍如斯，对伤害的耐受度，以及体力和灵力恢复大大超过普通修士。除却自身实力加强，生魄将赋予魁元“领域压迫”，又称为“威压”，当遇见普通修士，或是生魄弱小的其他魁元，会极大程度限制其实力施展，但威压对于参宿无用。由于过于敏感的灵识，生魄越强悍的魁元越容易出现“灵识暴动”，若没有参宿安抚，会导致其灵识损毁。3.参宿的识海是普通修士十倍甚至百倍，只有参宿可以疏解魁元的“灵识暴动”。4.在觉醒之后，无论是魁元还是参宿，都需要寻灵兽为生魄，一般有两种方法：一是灵兽自愿献灵，二是灵兽杀死后强行剥其灵魄。生魄将直接影响魁元“威压”的强弱，拥有愈强悍的生魄的魁元越难寻找相配的参宿。5.参宿都可在短时间内压制魁元的“灵识暴动”，但要完全疏解需要“灵犀相通”（结合）。灵犀建立条件苛刻，两人生魄必须相配，并且需要两人神交欲合，灵肉合一。灵犀建立后，两人灵识互通，魁元将不再受其他参宿气韵的影响，参宿同理，两人对彼此会产生强大且不可抗拒的吸引力。灵犀为终身制，除非一方死亡，或强行破除。6.将魁元（黑暗哨兵）是魁元中最强大的存在，极其稀少，会吸引异兽榜之上灵兽为其生魄，有强悍灵识（几乎不会产生灵识暴动），在参宿选择上没有下限，可同任何生魄的参宿灵犀相通。

summary: Lan Wangji was barely seventeen the day he became a god, his eyes burning with molten gold while his gaze never left Lan Xichen's, a silent promise passing between them.....Lan Zhan was barely six when he had sat at the steps of his mother's confinement and had stared silently into the night, heard the whispers of his seniors around him, their sorrowful and hungry gazes. He had been seven when the elders had told him,  as it is your elder brother's fate to be sect leader one day, Lan Zhan, so it is your fate to be a sect god.--And here is the thing: many cultivators -- most of the Lan sect elders and disciples included -- see it as a great honor, to be made into a god. Wen Ruohan proclaimed himself one, his age and powerful cultivation lending credit to the ruse, but this close to being one himself, Lan Wangji could see that it was not quite true. Could see that he was mortal still, and he'd told Lan Xichen as much, that they had a chance to defeat the sun if only they rallied together.But the truth is, Lan Wangji didn't see himself as much of a god, and felt no happiness at being turned into one, just as Lan Xichen felt no happiness losing the only brother he's ever had.

It sounds slightly odd, but Lan Zhan wants Wei Ying to have anything, everything, has since Wei Ying persistently annoyed his way into Lan Zhan’s heart when they were 15 and at school together and apparently, everything includes Netflix and chill with him. summary: In the ancient realm there was a soul who was known widely as Hanguang-Jun. He was known to be aloof and away from worldly beings. Seldom people knew him for who he was or what his heart truly yearned in reality. A man who loved dearly and in return lost everything when he cared for what the world thought of him, but when he received a second chance, to love again, to live again, to be united with the man who was born and reborn to be his, he didn't care anymore. summary: Wèi WúXiàn’s fingers gently pluck a gentian from his garden. He pulls it close against his chest in reminisce of what once was. He sighs, “Perhaps…” He shakes his head. He thinks he has gone crazy, for having hope.He thought that Lan Wang Ji would sigh, remove his hand and hug him tightly while repeating the same mantra of i’m sorry’s, only making him realize that he was indeed crazy and wrong. summary: Recueil d'OS canon écrits divers et variés. Probablement beaucoup d'introspections.2-Impossible : Wei Wuxian sait depuis longtemps que ce qui limite toujours l'invention dans les sectes, ce ne sont pas les traditions, ni les règles, ni le talent. Tout ces facteurs ont un rôle à jouer, évidemment. Mais la vraie limitation, c'est la capacité à penser ce qui est possible et ce qui ne l'est pas. Qui se sent capable de tenter ce qu'il pense absolument impossible ?3-Solitaire : Jiang Cheng est le fils de sa mère ; il en a les défauts et les qualité et c'est sur elles qu'il doit s'appuyer pour reconstruire sa secte. Que faire d'autre ? Sa sœur s'est mariée et Wei Ying n'est plus là, et il doit se résigner à être seul. Exploration-introspection du personnage.4-Le rubanLe ruban des Lan a toujours eu une double signification : preuve de leur maîtrise de soi et un gage d'amour. Les moralistes de la secte l'utilisent comme une injonction, les poètes comme un soupir languissant... Et Lan Wangji, plein de ces récits et de ces paradoxes, regarde sa famille et leur rapport à cet objet.

summary: He startles, glancing around. Wei Wuxian had just been right beside him. They hadn’t been speaking, after Wei Wuxian’s few abortive attempts at making conversation. Because Jiang Cheng hadn’t wanted to speak to him. He never wants to speak to him, ever again, because walking alongside Wei Wuxian, being on a night hunt with him— it’s too much. Even if he no longer wants Wei Wuxian dead, how can participate in these farces? How can he get so close to the thing he wants, only to remember he’ll never have it? He can’t let Wei Wuxian make casual conversation. He can’t allow him to weasel his way back into Jiang Cheng’s good graces, his heart. Because Jiang Cheng won’t survive it. He knows this very well. What starts as a simple competition during a night hunt quickly spirals out of control, leaving Jiang Cheng to confront his fears, his feelings, his inadequacies, and Wei Wuxian.

summary:
If he were just like Lan Wangji, Jiang Cheng could dismiss the nagging voice in his head that said he’s family, and you have close to nothing left. Jiang Cheng could have left the night hunt with the unanimous truth about Lan Sizhui: he wasn’t his family. He wasn’t like Wei Wuxian, he was moulded and shaped by Lan education to be the same stuffy, emotionless, powerhouse of a teenager Lan Wangji once was. He was just some kid, some future Lan leader, an heir, more Lan Wangji’s than Wei Wuxian’s, whatever the nature of their relationship may be. 
  
  But Lan Wangji would not have thrown himself in front of that sword. Lan Wangji would have never bled out on the floor to save Jiang Cheng from the imminent threat of death. Never in a million years would he do something as reckless and self-sacrificial.
  That was Wei Wuxian, through and through. Lan Sizhui was Wei Wuxian’s son. (or, in which Lan Sizhui is forced to stay in Lotus Pier for three weeks, and saves Jiang Cheng in more ways than one. Turns out stab wounds heal faster than 16 years of regret.)

summary: Lan WangJi had always thought he was most like the night, tranquil, cold... Forgotten. The moon stood alone, looking down on a slumbering world. But he… He had been like the sun. He had been vibrant, so full of life. He had been the chatter at the open market, the tart snap of tanghulu, the rush of flying. It seemed false, to remember him here, now, under the cover of night. However, there is a distinguishable lilt to it, an odd pitch that usually only results from the usage of a voice-changing spell. And although that queer shift in pitch is subtle—suggesting the user’s proficiency in skill at using this particular mode of disguise—it’s the fact that the other person is even attempting to camouflage himself that sets off the warning bells in Jiang Cheng’s head.The person that captured and brought him here is someone he knows. That’s why they had to disguise their voice. summary: “Slow burn?” Jiang Cheng scoffs as he reenters the room, shoving a drink unceremoniously at Wei Ying, “These two? More like enemies to lovers.”It does not upset Lan Wangji that Jiang Cheng says this. He does not expect much from the other man, not when he has never before shown any respect or deference to Lan Wangji’s relationship with Wei Ying. summary: “Fancy seeing you here!” Xichen calls, and Wangji carefully turns the two of them to face him with an expression of mild surprise. Bichen is tucked beneath one arm, with a bag hanging from that hand, while the other holds Yuan steady on his shoulders. He nods at the sight of Xichen; perhaps those who do not know him might think it a cold response, but Xichen knows him well enough to see the tiny smile that tugs briefly at the corner of his mouth.Yuan, his mouth already closing around the bun, brightens like the sun. He beams through an enormous bite and waves the bun cheerfully. A few seconds of industrious chewing later, he offers a crumby, “Hello Uncle Xichen!”“Good afternoon!” Xichen keeps his eyes on Yuan’s face, and carefully schools his expression into one of astonishment. summary: Lan Wangji, the powerful Second Alpha and Jade of the Gusu Lan pack, thought his fate had been sealed long ago when his father had arranged a marriage between him and a high ranking omega from the Lanling Jin pack. They will never make the mistake that he did. They will never marry for love. Qingheng-Jun’s bitter outlook on love poisoned the young alpha’s mind until he, too, viewed the sentiment with sourness. Lan Wangji had come up with a plan that, at the time, seemed full-proof. While inhaling his late mother’s fragrance, he decided that it would be the only scent that he would allow himself to cherish. From that day forward, he would force his beast to abhor the scent of all alphas and omegas, no matter their pack status. By the time he had grown into the title of Second Alpha, Lan Wangji had far out reached his goal. He could no longer smell the natural scent of any alpha or omega in his presence. Now, as the day of the wedding finally arrives, Lan Wangji sits alone in his Jinshi, the weight of his future lying heavily on his chest. There is a sword in his hand.
  
    The hilt is sized perfectly to his grip. This weapon was made for him. He holds it in grief, the weight of it almost too much to bear, all his failings stacked upon it. There is blood on the blade. The sword is thrust through another man’s chest. Blood covers pale robes, staining them red. There is blood on his hands as he grips the hilt. A croaked voice mutters, soft and too intimate for such a statement: “Er-ge, stay and die with me.”
  
    He looks up and for the first time he has had this dream, the face of the man saying it is not in shadow. There are wide eyes, fanned by dark lashes, and dark lips stained with blood.

summary: Jiang Cheng, his little brother´s other best friend, was sitting in a corner of the karaoke establishment they were in, silently nursing his vodka with a pensive look on his beautiful face (his preferred drink when he felt down and just wanted to forget-). His well-known frown was more prominent than usual, and the strict tight arch of his full lips spoke of him remembering something unpleasant. But it was not that what made Nie Mingjue worry about the other, no. It was his eyes. Those blue-grey eyes that seemed to become an alluring purple when hit by candlelight in the middle of night as thunder could be heard in the distance (always looking like some kind of avenging angel that only left their guard down when in-), but those eyes now seemed to be filled with so much sorrow and pain.  Yes, he had come to known those eyes intimately, all those years ago. The ones he had said goodbye to when he thought it would be for the best (still not wanting to believe the reason behind that sadness). But oh, how he regretted it now.

summary: The Nie sect’s ancestors were butchers; that lowly heritage is well known and widely celebrated, much to the not-entirely-concealed disdain of some of the more refined, gentlemanly sects. Butchers at home and butchers at war – everyone knows that.What’s rather less well known is that the third sect leader, colloquially known among his descendants as ‘that idiot’, rather heroically saved an imperial princess in battle and then – and this was why he was that idiot – married her. She was a proper princess, too, the true-born daughter of the emperor; other sects might see that as a good thing, since for all that cultivation sects saw themselves as being above petty things like the politics of the common folk, a princess was still a princess.The Nie did not.The reason for this was quite simple. What does a cultivation style that already incorporates an increased chance of death through anger most assuredly does not need?The blood of the eight-clawed dragon, that’s what.

summary: ¿Qué habría pasado si Jiang Fengmian nunca hubiera dado con el paradero de Wei Wuxian cuando se quedó huérfano en las calles?Wei Ying creció solo y por su cuenta. Las calles no son amables con los huérfanos y sin un mentor que le enseñara a cultivar los métodos apropiados, su estilo personal se volvió más bien caótico; su aparente habilidad nata para gobernar las energías a su alrededor, no obstante, le ha dado un espacio bajo el cuidado de Wen RuoHan.Mientras tanto, el mundo de los cultivadores está cayéndose a pedazos. El clan Wen logró absorber al clan Lanling Jin luego de que Jin Guangshan abandonara la junta de la hermandad de sectas para aliarse con Wen RuoHan, sabiendo que no podrían derrotarle, y bajo su comando ambos clanes se proclamaron sobre el resto. Casi todos los sobrevivientes y desertores se unificaron para formar una resistencia contra Qishan Wen y los remanentes de Lanling Jin. Los clanes se volvieron nómadas, perseguidos por los cazadores de rebeldes, enfrentándose en cruentas batallas en el camino.Los Wen habrían querido aplastarles a todos como cucarachas, pero destruir al enemigo desde su interior podría probarse ser una estrategia mejor.

summary: He startles, glancing around. Wei Wuxian had just been right beside him. They hadn’t been speaking, after Wei Wuxian’s few abortive attempts at making conversation. Because Jiang Cheng hadn’t wanted to speak to him. He never wants to speak to him, ever again, because walking alongside Wei Wuxian, being on a night hunt with him— it’s too much. Even if he no longer wants Wei Wuxian dead, how can participate in these farces? How can he get so close to the thing he wants, only to remember he’ll never have it? He can’t let Wei Wuxian make casual conversation. He can’t allow him to weasel his way back into Jiang Cheng’s good graces, his heart. Because Jiang Cheng won’t survive it. He knows this very well.What starts as a simple competition during a night hunt quickly spirals out of control, leaving Jiang Cheng to confront his fears, his feelings, his inadequacies, and Wei Wuxian.

summary: Wei Wuxian se esconde en Descanso en la Nube después de que Lan Wangji lo salvara en Torre Carpa. Convertidos en fugitivos de los clanes, ambos tratan de decidir qué harán a continuación. Sin embargo, y aunque deberían estar más preocupados por lo que ocurre a su alrededor, ninguno de los dos puede dejar de pensar en las consecuencias que implica el gesto que tuvo Lan Wangji al darle la espalda a todos para salvar a Wei Wuxian. Porque es evidente que lo que siente Hanguang-jun no es simple compañerismo. ¿Ha llegado el momento de enfrentarse a los sentimientos que tienen el uno por el otro? ¿O seguirán negando la evidencia, demasiado asustados de lo que podría ocurrir si lo hacen?Este fic retoma los últimos capítulos de la serie y trata de desarrollar entre escenas perdidas la relación romántica de Wei Wuxian y Lan Wangji que la adaptación no contempla, centrándose en la personalidad que tienen en la adaptación. El desarrollo diverge del canon de la novela y crea una nueva narrativa.

  “Including one specifically about not having any kind of spices in the kitchens, which feels really petty, if you ask me. And one stating, specifically, that no one is,” he mimics the low timbre of Lan Qiren’s voice and the way the older man strokes his beard even though he can’t be seen, “Do not approach or talk to Wei Wuxian.” He huffs out a breath, “Talk about making someone feel unwelcome, Zewu-Jun. I don’t know if I should be honoured or heartbroken that I have become so hated that I have been immortalised on your wall of rules.”
Lan Xichen is in isolation. Wei Wuxian visits him. Together they find their way back to happiness, to clarity and to home.

summary: Sometimes men are knives. Sometimes they wield them. Wen Ning had never wanted to be a knife. He had wanted to be a boy, and then a man. He had wanted his sister not to worry, to never be afraid. He had wanted to be strong enough that she wouldn’t search for bruises under his skin or sleep restless at his bedside through fevered nights. He did not think he would ever bruise again. He would not heal again, never watch purpled and yellowed flesh fade back to flushed, whole skin. He would never wake to her hand cooling his forehead. Wen Ning would just go find a little river, after bad fights, and wash himself off gently. He’d sew himself up, a stitch at a time, and tell himself that because the pain felt different now it didn’t count as pain at all. ---Podfic for dirgewithoutmusic.

He took it knowing full well its effects, knowing full well with it he would give in to the crushing clawing need that burned in his veins. That overwhelming desire to kiss and possess Wei Ying for his own. The hot, blistering kiss they shared later that night was inevitable just like the prickling, irritating way they interacted with each other. Every harsh word just as intense as the kiss that burned their mouths. When Lan WangJi had found himself in the passionate, irrational embrace of the YiLing Patriarch, he had no idea how he had gotten there; the hard, velvety press of those clever lips against him had robbed him of his mind, of any semblance of reason he could have ever had. Instead he surrendered himself to his desire, to the desire to possess this man who seemed so intangible, so transient and so completely untouchable.

It burned in him, the idea of the two of them, of Xue Yang’s hands, bloodstained, stroking over Xingchen’s skin, touching him, inside him—“I told Xue Yang that we all have pasts, that only who you become matters. Who you choose to be now,” Xiao Xingchen had told him, that first day. “Do you not agree? Is there not a possibility for change, for new life, in everyone?”“But—him?” Song Lan had said, Fuxue vibrating in his grip with his need to punish Xue Yang, to separate him from Xiao Xingchen. His whole life taken from him, all the innocents murdered, everyone he’d grown up with, and the man responsible, the man who’d blinded Song Lan--“We either mean it, or we don’t,” Xingchen had said. summary: Вэй Усянь – охотник, как и его мать.Он с самого детства учился отвечать зову Охоты. Он выжил и стал самым искусным убийцей своего поколения, и даже если ему пришлось учиться сражаться самому, даже если он, его брат и сестра – последние охотники в городе, он знает на чьей он стороне, что нужно делать и кто его враг. Он всегда помнит, что Охота может пойти не по плану, но раньше и представить себе не мог, что его жизнь спасёт вампир. Без всякого милосердия или беспокойства – с одним только равнодушием.И не то чтобы он этого хотел, да и желания объединяться с одним из существ, для убийства которых его растили, у него не было, но в их маленьком мире что-то происходит. А когда обстоятельства того требуют, Вэй Усянь усмирит свою гордыню и извлечёт свою выгоду. И, может быть, по ходу дела осознать, что он многого не знает о вампирах.

summary: The boy puts his fan away and points at Jiang Cheng. He twirls his finger in a slow circle. “You’re going to like me…” the boy says. “You’re going to like me.”He tilts his head as he looks up at Jiang Cheng. “Did it work?”-Jiang Cheng doesn’t try to be a hero. He keeps his head down, does his job, and keeps the two other people he’s claimed as family safe. He’s not like Wei Wuxian, who aimed for heroism and instead spirals deeper into a world of secrets and dark magic with each passing day.Life can’t be simple. Not when Jiang Cheng dreams of a woman who single handedly ended a war nearly two decades earlier. Not when there’s a Sorceress, wielding an ancient and terrifying power, bringing entire nations to their knees. Not when Wei Wuxian forsakes his family for the sake of someone he’s never even met.Not when Nie Huaisang takes Jiang Cheng by the hand and waltzes with him as if he was someone who mattered. Not when that dreamy artist turned resistance fighter inherits magic capable of unraveling time itself. And certainly not when Jiang Cheng still has to learn just why love makes people attempt the impossible.

summary: Every once in a while, he stops to listen to the different noise and look over Lotus Pier, peering into the distance like he’s waiting for something—which he’s not. He’s not waiting for anything, for anyone. But no matter how loud it gets sometimes, and how much he can fool himself into thinking this was sixteen years ago when he closes his eyes and listens to the yells of the vendors and the water lapping against the shore, his chest is still empty. That’s something he doesn’t think about, either. He knows why, but it’s hard to get out, and he’d rather sit in his room and bark orders at his disciples and not look for anyone he doesn’t want to see, or thinks he doesn’t want to see, when he has to ride up to Gusu.  Jiang Cheng is planning on avoiding Wei Wuxian after things blow over, but life has a way of fucking plans up, and so Wei Wuxian comes to tell him that he's getting married to Lan Wangji. By throwing himself into half-planning a wedding and having conversations with his nephew(s) and other members of Wei Wuxian's found family, Jiang Cheng navigates through his complicated feelings and realises that something new can be built with his brother, and that he is far less alone than he had thought.

summary: La famosa araña violeta, cuyo nombre causaba miedo, su firme voz estremecía a los discípulos y su arma espiritual, Zidian; un chispeante látigo púrpura, podía causar terror en sus contrincantes.Todos la conocen como una mujer fuerte y de carácter imponente. Pero... ¿alguien sabe lo que oculta tras sus ojos fieros y la dureza en sus palabras?  Proveniente de Meishan Yu, mantiene en alto su rostro a pesar de su decepción amorosa, Yu Ziyuan está dispuesta a seguir adelante por ella y por el futuro de sus hijos. Un niño harapiento de ojos grises interrumpe su hogar trayendo vagos recuerdos y una serie de chismes que le hierven la sangre. No sabe manejar sus sentimientos, desquita su furia en palabras venenosas. Pero, muy en el fondo... todo es diferente. ¿Un secreto? Yu Ziyuan realmente fue quien crió a Wei Wuxian. No es la mejor madre. Todo humano es imperfecto y ella no es la excepción. Cometió muchos errores y ciertamente, sus palabras no concuerdan con los sentimientos de su corazón. Ella huye de la tristeza de esos ojos grises, aún así lo crió, lo vio crecer, lo cuidó ¡nadie vendrá a dañar a su hijo adoptivo! Ella es Yu Ziyuan, matriarca y líder de YunmengJiang.

summary: Sometimes men are knives. Sometimes they wield them. Wen Ning had never wanted to be a knife. He had wanted to be a boy, and then a man. He had wanted his sister not to worry, to never be afraid. He had wanted to be strong enough that she wouldn’t search for bruises under his skin or sleep restless at his bedside through fevered nights. He did not think he would ever bruise again. He would not heal again, never watch purpled and yellowed flesh fade back to flushed, whole skin. He would never wake to her hand cooling his forehead. Wen Ning would just go find a little river, after bad fights, and wash himself off gently. He’d sew himself up, a stitch at a time, and tell himself that because the pain felt different now it didn’t count as pain at all.
